title: Crispy Garlic Chicken Thighs
seoTitle: One-Pot Chicken and Rice | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: One pot, hard to mess up
subtitle: One pot, hard to mess up
description: One pot, hard to mess up. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.
equipment: Large Dutch oven with tight lid

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Crispy Garlic Chicken Thighs in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on. Double-check seasoning after scaling — crew palates run salty after long shifts, so taste the first portion before opening the line. Use Yellow onion, diced, Fresh parsley, chopped as listed — measure each before heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch chicken. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Season and brown chicken
steps.instruction: Pat chicken thighs dry; season all over with salt and pepper. Brown skin-side down in butter in a large Dutch oven over medium-high 6–8 minutes until golden. Flip briefly, then remove to a plate — you are building flavor, not finishing here.

steps.title: Sweat onion and toast rice
steps.instruction: In the same pot, cook onion in the chicken fat 4–5 minutes until soft. Stir in garlic and rice; toast 2 minutes until edges look translucent.

steps.title: Add broth and nestle chicken
steps.instruction: Pour in chicken broth, thyme, and bay leaves. Nestle chicken skin-side up on the rice. Bring to a simmer, then cover tightly and reduce heat to low. Target 165°F at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Simmer until rice is tender
steps.instruction: Cook covered 22–25 minutes without lifting the lid — steam escapes and rice goes crunchy. Chicken should read 165°F in the thickest part; rice should be tender and broth absorbed.

steps.title: Steam vegetables and rest
steps.instruction: Scatter peas and carrots over the top; cover 5 minutes off heat so vegetables steam. Discard bay leaves. Fluff rice with a fork, taking care not to shred chicken.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Crispy Garlic Chicken Thighs onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Scale for larger halls
steps.instruction: When cooking for more than 8 firefighters, split into two pans halfway through so the bottom layer does not overcook while the top waits — duplicate mise en place if you double batches.

steps.title: Serve one-pot portions
steps.instruction: Plate chicken over rice on sheet trays or serve family-style from the pot. Finish with parsley and lemon wedges. Keep the seasoning simple — thyme, salt, and pepper only.

proTips: Assign one cook to proteins and one to sides — rookies stay on timing, not multitasking.
Prep all mise en place before the bell — this meal wins on organization, not speed hacks.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
Pull chicken at 160°F and let carryover hit 165°F — dry breast ruins crew morale.
tonightSpread: Fluff rice with a fork at the table — chicken thighs stay skin-side up for crisp skin.
Lemon wedges and parsley on the side; no hot sauce bar needed for this one.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: One pot, hard to mess up. A hall pick for tight shifts — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
mealPrepNotes: Minimal prep — chop aromatics before shift change so you can cook as soon as the board quiets.
substitutions: Chicken thighs ↔ breasts (thighs forgive overcooking on the flat-top).
